name: Project Manager (PM) in a PM²-Agile Project
one_liner: Still runs the project; hands facilitation to TeCo and priorities to PrOw.
purpose: When PM²-Agile is introduced within PM², the new roles take on some responsibilities usually assigned to the Project Manager, but the PM role is not removed. Methodology compliance becomes shared with the Team Coordinator, team and progress management passes to the self-organising A-PCT, and the Product Owner becomes the permanent point of contact for business stakeholders. The PM remains responsible for the whole project and stays Accountable in every PM²-Agile artefact RAM.

items: The whole project and its deliverables — the PM² role is not deleted
The Project Charter (Responsible) and the Project Handbook
Accountability for every A-PCT artefact: handbook, work plan, WIL, plans, reports
The Project Status Report, fed from the Development Status Report
Escalated impediments raised by the team via the Team Coordinator
Whether development plans align with the Project Charter and project milestones
When to intervene, with the Business Manager, on misaligned expectations
Approves and authorises the A-PCT's artefacts as the Accountable role
Iteration Planning, Review and Retrospective — as a regular Agile Team Member
Informed of the Iteration Goal and of Daily Stand-up outcomes
Informed of the outputs of every Work Items List ceremony
Project follow-up meetings, demos and deliverables acceptance events

Assign and monitor each team member's work until it is complete
Turn the Daily Stand-up into a status update meeting
Set or reorder the Work Items List — the PrOw prioritises it
Hold methodology compliance alone — it is shared with the Team Coordinator

fields.what: The PM educates the team on PM² per the Project Handbook; the TeCo guarantees agile values per the Development Handbook.
fields.pollux: You keep PM² compliance; Lovelace keeps the agile practice honest.

fields.what: Participates in Iteration Planning, Review and Retrospective as a regular Agile Team Member while the TeCo facilitates.
fields.pollux: You attend the review as one voice among several, not as chair.

fields.what: PM² makes the PM ensure efficient use of resources; in PM²-Agile the self-organising A-PCT manages its own work.
fields.who: A-PCT via the Development Work Plan
fields.pollux: You stop assigning tasks; the team plans each two-week iteration itself.

fields.what: The change frees the PM to focus on the problems and impediments the A-PCT identifies via the Team Coordinator.
fields.pollux: You unblock the national-authority access decision, not the sprint board.

fields.what: The PrOw becomes the permanent contact between requester and provider and aligns scope and time-frame expectations.
fields.pollux: Curie handles the quarterly requirement churn from Risk, Finance and the Board.

fields.what: The PM, together with the Business Manager, may intervene when expectations are misaligned or the PrOw and the team cannot reach consensus.
fields.pollux: Conflict 3 — you and Hopper step in over Release 2 scope only if consensus fails.

fields.what: Must be aware how the A-PCT plans to manage development and ensure the Project Handbook captures the relevant information.
fields.pollux: You approve the handbook baselined 27 Nov 2028 before the RfE gate.

fields.f: Accountable for the Development Work Plan
fields.what: Must know how the team plans to deliver and how that aligns with the overall project milestones.
fields.who: TeCo Responsible; PrOw owns the WIL part
fields.pollux: You show Gantt that WIL, Release Plan and Iteration Plan are the schedule.

fields.f: Accountable for the Work Items List
fields.what: Must be aware how the WIL, as part of the Development Work Plan, aligns with the scope defined in the Project Charter.
fields.who: PrOw is Responsible; TeCo consulted for consistency
fields.pollux: You check Curie's list still delivers success criteria SC1 to SC5.

fields.what: Accountable for alignment between the delivery strategy in the Release Plan and the project vision and milestones.
fields.pollux: You hold the four releases against the 20 Dec 2029 final release date.

fields.what: Accountable for ensuring the iteration goal aligns with the Release Plan strategy and the Project Charter.
fields.pollux: You confirm iteration 1 on 08 Jan 2029 serves Release 1 in March.

fields.what: Understands the essential architectural decisions and constraints and relays infrastructure needs to hosting services.
fields.pollux: You carry Einstein's hosting constraints to ESM IT for the portal.

fields.what: Accountable for the team's testing approach and its alignment with deliverables' acceptance, and for the deployment approach.
fields.who: ATeMs draft the Test Plan; TeCo the Deployment Plan
fields.pollux: You align testing with acceptance ahead of transition on 31 Jan 2030.

fields.f: Accountable for the Development Status Report
fields.what: Must be aware how the A-PCT is progressing and ensure the Project Status Report captures the relevant information.
fields.pollux: Lovelace's report feeds your Project Status Report to the steering layer.

fields.what: In PM², the PM is Responsible for the Project Charter, with the PSC accountable and the BM supporting.
fields.pollux: You wrote the charter approved on 12 Oct 2028, before the RfP gate.

traps: PM²-Agile does not delete the PM; the TeCo is not a renamed Project Manager.
The PM attends ceremonies as a regular ATeM — the TeCo facilitates them.
The Daily Stand-up is not a status meeting; the PM is merely informed.
The PM is Accountable for the Work Items List even though the PrOw is Responsible.
The PM no longer assigns and monitors individual work; the team self-organises.
